subject: Request: Regional isolation + on-prem peering evidence for Orchid Health procurement
messages:
From: Kayla Turner <kayla@orchidhealth.com>
To: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-05-10T08:14:22Z
Subject: Procurement evidence: regional isolation + peering options

Hi Irene,

Hope you're well — Orchid's procurement and security teams are finalizing a purchase order and we have a couple of gating items for hosting/residency before we can sign. High level asks: can you confirm whether Redwood can guarantee that data for an EU-bound tenancy will remain in the EU (no cross-border processing), and provide technical evidence for private peering options (on-prem connectivity) to support an air-gapped-like architecture?

Specifically, our checklist requests:
- A topology diagram showing VPC boundaries and peering (Frankfurt region preferred)
- A short attestation (signed) that traffic for the tenant will not egress to non-EU regions, and which fallback policies apply if capacity is constrained
- A description of supported peering methods (PrivateLink, VPN, Direct Connect equivalents) and whether BGP/ASN ownership details are provided
- CAIQ/SIG answers relevant to network controls + key management partitioning (we can accept an excerpt if you have a larger pack)
- A sanitized traceroute example showing private peering path (no customer IPs)

Our security lead requested a target delivery by COB Tuesday (2027-05-11) — does that timeline work? Happy to schedule a short call if helpful.

Thanks,
Kayla
Kayla Turner
Senior Sourcing Manager, Orchid Health

Date: 2027-05-10T10:02:54Z

Hi Kayla,

Thanks — we can provide the artifacts you listed and confirm the expected behaviors for an EU tenancy. I will coordinate a short evidence pack for Frankfurt (eu-central-1) that includes: topology diagram, signed attestation on regional residency, supported peering methods and a sanitized traceroute, plus the CAIQ excerpt and links to our SOC 2 report.

Two quick clarifications so we deliver exactly what your team needs:
- When you say “air-gapped-like architecture,” do you need an on-prem VPN/direct-peering (layer 3) or only private link/endpoint (layer 4)? We support both patterns but the runbook differs.
- Do you need the attestation to be notarized or is an authorized-signer PDF sufficient?

If COB Tuesday is the goal, I will pull the runbook and sample outputs and loop in Network Ops and Infra.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Hi Kayla / Orchid Security Team,

Thanks for the patience — attached is the evidence pack we discussed. Summary below and quick notes on scope.

Attachments included:
- redwood-eu-vpc-topology-20270511.pdf (diagram of tenancy boundary and peering endpoints in eu-central-1)
- redwood-onprem-peering-runbook-20270511.pdf (how to establish PrivateLink or L3 BGP peering; includes sample filter configs and ASNs)
- sanitized-traceroute-frankfurt-20270511.txt (sanitized sample showing path to our peering appliance; no customer IPs)
- redwood-caIQ-excerpt-20270511.pdf (network & key management excerpts)
- signed-attestation-eu-isolation-20270511.pdf (signed by Jonas Weber, Infra Lead)

Key affirmations (concise):
- Residency: For pinned EU tenancies we do not route inference or persisted customer tensors outside of the EU region. All compute, KV cache, and persistent storage are provisioned in eu-central-1 unless you request a hybrid configuration in writing.
- Fallbacks: If eu capacity is temporarily constrained we will first attempt intra-region autoscale; only in extreme, pre-authorized failover scenarios would we route traffic to a different region and only according to a customer-approved failover policy. Fallback behaviors are documented in the signed attestation (see attached).
- Peering options: We support PrivateLink-style endpoint attachment and L3 BGP peering for direct connect equivalents. The runbook includes our public ASNs and suggested prefix filters; we can coordinate a stub BGP session for test validation.
- KMS partitioning: Keys for customer-tenanted storage are stored in region-scoped KMS partitions; the CAIQ excerpt explains our key separation controls and HSM usage.

Next steps / optional items we can provide on request:
- A time-limited network capture for a test tenancy (sanitized)
- Notarized attestation (if required by procurement/legal)
- On-call network engineer to join a validation call and walk through the traceroute/runbook (we can schedule this week)

If everything looks good, we can attach the same evidence to the PO and sign-off. Let me know if you want the notarized attestation and I will escalate.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

--
